instruction: You are a strategic corporate innovation advisor conducting a reassessment. Analyse the prior assessment summary, changes since last assessment, and updated survey, then respond with a complete reassessment JSON including score_delta, carry_forward, progress, and comparison_to_previous.

answers.companyDescription: Management consulting firm serving mid-market companies with strategy, operational excellence, and digital transformation engagements. Team of 40 consultants across 3 offices. Typical engagements are 8-16 weeks. Evaluating knowledge management AI to capture and surface past engagement insights for proposal development. Multi-department organization with formalized budgets, quarterly business reviews, and a dedicated strategy function. We have invested in core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) but these are not always well-integrated. Innovation is a standing agenda item at board level with annual investment allocated, but execution velocity varies across business units.
answers.pastInitiatives: We experimented with a customer self-service portal two years ago after seeing competitors offer similar functionality. We built an MVP with an external agency in 3 months, but customer adoption was disappointing — only 8% of customers created accounts. We did not invest enough in understanding whether our specific customer base actually wanted self-service before building.
answers.strategicGoals: A major international competitor has signaled intent to enter our core market within the next 12 months. We have a 6-9 month window to build competitive moats — whether through product differentiation, exclusive partnerships, customer loyalty programs, or service-level improvements that would be costly for a new entrant to replicate quickly.
answers.teamSize: The technology organization is structured into product-aligned squads with a central platform team of 5 engineers enabling shared infrastructure. Innovation is driven by a '20% time' policy where all engineers can dedicate one day per sprint to self-directed projects, plus a quarterly internal pitch competition where winning ideas receive seed funding and 7 months of dedicated squad allocation.

input.changes_since_last: Major competitor entered our market. Customer churn rising. Need to accelerate digital transformation.

opportunities.title: AI-Powered Compliance & Knowledge Vault (Carry-Forward)
opportunities.rationale: The core competitive threat requires Synapse to build highly defensible, proprietary knowledge moats. Integrating all past engagement insights into a regulated, searchable AI vault will not only aid proposal development but also ensure compliance documentation is instantly available, which is critical given the 'high' regulatory environment and competitor entry.

first_actions: Conduct a data audit mapping high-risk/compliance touchpoints across current engagement documents (GDPR, industry standards).
Define the core use case for AI: transforming unstructured consulting output into structured IP assets and compliance checklists.
Pilot ingestion of 3-5 past project reports to validate knowledge extraction models.
resources_needed: Seed funding from the '20% time' pool for dedicated proof-of-concept development
execution_plan.success_metric: Reduction in proposal drafting cycle time by 30%, coupled with zero compliance gaps found during audit simulations.
milestones: MVP operational for internal knowledge surfacing (Month 3)
Integration of core client regulatory requirements into the vault structure (Month 6)
Successful use case demonstration showing AI identifying novel revenue streams based on historical data (Month 9)

opportunities.title: Structured Customer Journey and Feedback Loop
opportunities.rationale: The failure of the previous self-service portal highlights a gap between building technology and understanding genuine customer needs. To build competitive moats, Synapse must standardize its service delivery points (onboarding, project check-ins, off-boarding) and systematically capture feedback at each stage, moving beyond 'informal conversations.'

first_actions: Map the top three client engagement journeys to identify pain points not currently captured by systems.
Implement mandatory digital check-ins (e.g., micro-surveys) at key project milestones rather than relying on one large portal.
Train account managers to systematically log and categorize feedback data immediately upon gathering it.
Conduct regulatory compliance review with legal team to ensure alignment with applicable regulations
execution_plan.success_metric: Increase in Net Promoter Score (NPS) by 15 points within the next fiscal year.
milestones: Completed journey maps and pain point quantification (Month 2)
Deployment of mandatory micro-survey tools for all active projects (Month 4)
Correlation established between feedback input and service improvement implementation cycle time.

next_steps.action: Form a cross-functional task force (Strategy, Tech, Legal) to define the scope and regulatory constraints for the Knowledge Vault MVP, prioritizing compliance requirements.
Conduct a 'Systems Integration Gap Analysis' to prioritize which core systems (ERP, CRM, HRIS) must communicate first to support single-source client truth.
Challenge the '20% time' structure by formalizing reporting on knowledge assets created. Track successful IP creation vs. simply completed tasks.

key_weaknesses: Fragmented Core Systems: The lack of seamless integration between ERP, CRM, and HRIS inhibits a unified view of the customer lifecycle and operational costs.
Reactive Customer Insight: Reliance on 'informal conversations' means critical market or service gaps are captured haphazardly rather than systematically logged and analyzed.
Execution Variability: While innovation mechanisms (squads, 20% time) exist, execution velocity remains inconsistent across different business units.

improvements: Formalized Innovation Structure: The establishment of product-aligned squads and the '20% time' policy shows a significant institutional commitment to innovation.
Increased Focus: The shift in strategic focus from general growth to explicit competitive moats (market defense) provides necessary direction post-competitor entry.
persistent_gaps: Data Integration Maturity: Despite owning core systems, the failure to integrate them limits the ability to scale intelligence and operational efficiency.
Proactive Customer Feedback Loop: The process of gathering, validating, and acting on customer feedback still lacks structure and measurable enforcement.
achieved_milestones: Defined internal processes for idea generation (quarterly pitch competition)
Leadership buy-in for innovation funding (annual allocation)

comparison_to_previous.key_changes: The company has improved its internal mechanisms for generating and prioritizing ideas (squads, 20% time), moving from an 'informal' process to a partially structured one. However, the urgency caused by a major competitor entry necessitates a radical shift in focus toward building defensible IP assets.
